question_text: Which of the following inputs is SAFE to paste directly into a non-approved external AI tool when preparing a client briefing?
scenario_text: You are preparing a briefing note for an upcoming review meeting with Crestwood Logistics Pty Ltd. You have access to their latest audited financials, an internal risk rating of 'Watch', a draft term sheet, and a publicly available industry report on freight logistics trends. You want to use an AI tool to help structure the briefing quickly.

options.label: A
options.text: The publicly available industry report on freight logistics trends, with no client-specific details added.

options.label: B
options.text: The client's audited financial statements, since they are already signed off and filed.

options.label: C
options.text: The internal risk rating note, because it is only one line of text and unlikely to cause harm.

options.label: D
options.text: The draft term sheet, because it has not yet been executed and is therefore not a final document.

question_text: The prompt below was used to prepare for a client renewal conversation but produced a vague, unhelpful response. Diagnose the prompting weaknesses and rewrite it as a stronger prompt that would generate a more useful output for an RM.
scenario_text:
An RM used this prompt before a facility renewal meeting:

'Help me prepare for a meeting with a client about renewing their loan.'

The AI returned a generic list of 'tips for client meetings' that was not useful for the RM's specific situation. The client is a mid-market construction company with a $3M working capital facility up for annual review. The RM wants to anticipate objections, identify upsell opportunities, and prepare 3 tailored talking points about the value the bank has delivered over the past year.

criteria.name: Diagnosis of prompt weaknesses
criteria.description: Learner correctly identifies at least two specific weaknesses: missing role/persona, no sector or client context, no specific output requested, and no constraints on format or purpose.

criteria.name: Quality of rewritten prompt
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt includes: a role frame (RM preparing for renewal), abstracted client context (mid-market construction, working capital facility), specific outputs requested (objection anticipation, upsell opportunities, value talking points), and a clear format instruction.

question_text: An AI tool drafts the following sentence for inclusion in a credit memo: 'Vantara Foods has consistently demonstrated strong liquidity management, with a current ratio well above industry benchmarks.' What is the most important critical evaluation step before including this in the memo?
scenario_text: You used an approved AI tool to help draft sections of a credit memo for Vantara Foods (a fictional client). The AI generated the sentence above based on your abstracted prompt describing the client as a 'food manufacturer with stable working capital.' You are about to paste it into the memo for submission to the credit committee.

options.label: A
options.text: Verify the claim against the client's actual financial data — confirm the current ratio figure and check it against a credible industry benchmark before including it.

options.label: B
options.text: Check that the sentence is grammatically correct and professionally worded before pasting it in.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask the AI to regenerate the sentence with more specific language to make it sound more authoritative.

options.label: D
options.text: Accept the sentence as accurate because it matches the general description you provided in your prompt.

question_text: An AI tool produced the portfolio insight summary below. Evaluate the quality of the data reasoning and identify any decisions an RM should NOT make based solely on this output, explaining why.
scenario_text:
AI-generated portfolio insight summary:

'Analysis of your portfolio indicates that clients in the retail sector are your lowest-performing segment by revenue contribution. These clients have the highest average cost-to-serve and the lowest product cross-sell ratio. Based on this, it is recommended that you deprioritise retail clients in your outreach plan and focus resources on manufacturing and logistics clients, who show stronger revenue metrics and higher facility utilisation.'

Your task: (1) Identify at least two data reasoning problems or missing considerations in this analysis. (2) Explain what decisions an RM should not make based solely on this AI output, and why.

criteria.name: Identification of data reasoning gaps
criteria.description: Learner identifies at least two specific gaps: e.g., the analysis ignores strategic value of retail relationships (referrals, tenure, growth potential), does not account for individual client variation within the segment, and may be based on incomplete or point-in-time data.

criteria.name: Decisions the RM should not make solely on this output
criteria.description: Learner correctly identifies that the RM should not deprioritise or reduce service to retail clients, reallocate portfolio resources, or make any client-facing decisions based solely on this AI summary — and explains that such decisions require human judgement, relationship context, and management input.

question_text: An RM wants to use AI to prepare a client intelligence summary before an annual review meeting. Which approach best demonstrates effective use of AI for relationship intelligence while staying within responsible AI boundaries?
scenario_text: You have an annual review meeting next week with the CEO of Driftwood Packaging Co., a long-standing client. You want to walk in with a sharp understanding of their business context, recent industry developments, and potential needs. You have access to publicly available news, the company's published annual report, and your own (sanitised) notes from previous meetings.

options.label: A
options.text: Prompt the AI with publicly available information (industry news, published annual report excerpts, sector trends) and your sanitised meeting notes to generate a structured pre-meeting intelligence brief covering business context, likely priorities, and suggested conversation angles.

options.label: B
options.text: Paste the client's full CRM record including internal risk ratings and deal history into the AI tool to get the most comprehensive intelligence summary possible.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask the AI to generate a client profile from scratch using only the company name, since AI tools have access to up-to-date business databases.

options.label: D
options.text: Use the AI to write a summary of the client's financial performance based on figures you recall from internal credit reports, without checking the source.

question_text: An RM uses AI to draft a follow-up email to a client after a difficult conversation about a declined credit application. Which of the following best describes the correct approach to using the AI draft?
scenario_text: You had a tense call with the CFO of Irongate Civil Pty Ltd after their facility increase request was declined by the credit committee. You want to send a professional, empathetic follow-up email that acknowledges their disappointment, explains the next steps, and keeps the relationship intact. You use an approved AI tool to draft the email.

options.label: A
options.text: Review the AI draft carefully, adjust the tone to reflect your genuine relationship with the CFO, verify that all stated next steps are accurate, and ensure no confidential credit committee reasoning is inadvertently disclosed before sending.

options.label: B
options.text: Send the AI draft immediately — it will be more professionally worded than anything you could write quickly, and speed matters after a difficult conversation.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask the AI to make the email more persuasive so the client feels the decision was the right one, without changing any factual content.

options.label: D
options.text: Use the AI draft as the final version but add the client's name and your signature, since personalisation is sufficient review for a routine follow-up.

question_text: Which of the following inputs is safe to include verbatim in an your organization's approved AI tool prompt without any abstraction or modification?
scenario_text: You are an Underwriter preparing a risk summary for a new transaction involving Thornfield Agri-Export Inc. You have four documents available: an internal client file note with payment history and risk commentary, a publicly available trade credit rating report published by a recognised ratings agency, a draft term sheet with proposed covenant thresholds, and an internal memo showing the deal's preliminary risk rating and rationale. You want to use an your organization's approved AI tool to help structure your analysis.

options.label: A
options.text: The publicly available trade credit rating report sourced from the ratings agency's published website.

options.label: B
options.text: The internal client file note, because it is stored on Apex Trade Finance's secure internal system.

options.label: C
options.text: The draft term sheet, because the deal has not yet been approved and no client has signed it.

options.label: D
options.text: The internal risk rating memo, because it contains analytical reasoning rather than raw financial figures.

question_text: Review the prompt below, which an Underwriter used to draft a covenant analysis section. Identify at least two specific structural weaknesses that reduce the quality of the AI output, and rewrite the prompt to address those weaknesses.
scenario_text:
An Underwriter submitted the following prompt to an your organization's approved AI tool:

---
"Analyse the covenants for this deal and tell me if they are appropriate."
---

The AI returned a two-sentence response stating that covenants are generally important for credit risk management and that leverage and interest coverage ratios are commonly used. The Underwriter found this unhelpful. Diagnose the prompt's weaknesses and produce an improved version.

criteria.name: Diagnosis of prompt weaknesses
criteria.description: Identifies at least two specific structural weaknesses: e.g., no context about the borrower or transaction type, no definition of 'appropriate,' no output format specified, no analytical criteria provided, no role framing, and no abstracted inputs supplied to ground the analysis.

criteria.name: Quality of rewritten prompt
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt includes role framing or context, specifies the type of transaction and borrower profile (abstracted), defines what 'appropriate' means in underwriting terms (e.g., aligned with leverage profile, sector norms), requests a structured output, and includes a constraint on handling missing information.

question_text: An AI tool has generated a financial risk summary for a borrower in the renewable energy sector. Which of the following responses represents the most appropriate underwriter behaviour when reviewing this output before including it in a credit paper?
scenario_text: You used an your organization's approved AI tool to draft the 'Financial Risk' section of a credit paper for a solar project developer. The AI output states: 'The borrower's debt service coverage ratio of 1.35x is within acceptable range for project finance transactions in this sector, and the leverage profile is consistent with investment-grade issuers.' You do not recall providing the DSCR figure in your prompt, and you know the borrower's actual leverage is higher than investment-grade norms.

options.label: A
options.text: Verify the DSCR figure against the source financial model, correct the leverage characterisation based on your own analysis, and revise the section before including it in the credit paper.

options.label: B
options.text: Accept the output as a reasonable approximation since AI tools are trained on large datasets and sector benchmarks are likely accurate.

options.label: C
options.text: Delete only the leverage sentence and keep the DSCR statement, since one error does not invalidate the rest of the AI-generated content.

options.label: D
options.text: Flag the section as 'AI-generated' in the credit paper so reviewers know to apply their own judgement, without making any changes yourself.

question_text: Review the AI-generated analysis excerpt below, which was produced to support a credit decision. Identify at least two analytical weaknesses or data reasoning errors that an Underwriter should correct before relying on this output, and explain what additional analysis or data would be needed.
scenario_text:
An Underwriter used an your organization's approved AI tool to analyse an abstracted borrower profile. The AI produced the following excerpt for the 'Financial Assessment' section:

---
"The borrower's revenue has grown at an average of 12% per year over the past three years, indicating strong business momentum. The current ratio of 1.8x suggests adequate short-term liquidity. Based on these indicators, the borrower demonstrates a solid financial profile consistent with investment-grade characteristics. The debt service coverage ratio is not provided but is assumed to be sufficient given the revenue growth trend."
---

criteria.name: Identification of analytical weaknesses
criteria.description: Identifies at least two specific analytical weaknesses: e.g., revenue growth alone does not indicate creditworthiness without profitability or margin data; 'investment-grade' characterisation is unsupported by the data provided; the DSCR assumption is a hallucinated inference not grounded in any provided figure; the current ratio alone is insufficient to assess liquidity without context on payables, inventory quality, or cash position.

criteria.name: Additional analysis or data requirements
criteria.description: Identifies what additional data or analysis is needed: e.g., actual DSCR from the financial model, EBITDA margin and net income trends, leverage ratio, cash flow from operations, and sector benchmarks to contextualise the current ratio and growth rate before any creditworthiness conclusion can be drawn.

question_text: An Underwriter is preparing for a first meeting with a new financial institution partner to discuss a potential risk-sharing arrangement. Which use of AI is most appropriate for building relationship intelligence ahead of this meeting?
scenario_text: You are an Underwriter preparing for an introductory meeting with Meridian Trade Finance Bank, a regional bank seeking to co-insure a portfolio of export receivables. You have access to the bank's publicly available annual report, a press release about their recent trade finance expansion, and an internal briefing note from the deal team. You want to use AI to help you prepare.

options.label: A
options.text: Use an your organization's approved AI tool to synthesise publicly available information about the bank's trade finance strategy, recent announcements, and regional focus to prepare informed questions and identify potential alignment with Apex Trade Finance's mandate.

options.label: B
options.text: Paste the internal deal team briefing note into a general AI chatbot to generate a relationship summary, since the note contains the most relevant context for the meeting.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask the AI to predict the bank's risk appetite and likely negotiating positions based on their public profile, and treat the output as a reliable basis for your meeting strategy.

options.label: D
options.text: Use AI to draft a relationship history summary by asking it to recall previous Apex Trade Finance interactions with Meridian Trade Finance Bank from its training data.

question_text: An Underwriter has used an AI tool to draft a section of a credit paper. Which of the following practices best reflects responsible and effective use of AI-augmented communication in this context?
scenario_text: You have used an your organization's approved AI tool to draft the 'Transaction Overview' section of a credit paper for a structured trade finance deal. The AI-generated draft is well-written and covers the main structural elements. However, you notice it uses generic language about the guarantee structure that does not accurately reflect the specific risk-sharing arrangement in this deal, and it omits the rationale for Apex Trade Finance's involvement.

options.label: A
options.text: Edit the draft to correct the guarantee structure description, add Apex Trade Finance mandate rationale, verify all factual claims, and ensure the final section reflects your professional judgement before submitting.

options.label: B
options.text: Submit the AI draft as written since it is well-structured and the approval committee will identify any inaccuracies during their review.

options.label: C
options.text: Add a footnote stating 'drafted with AI assistance' and submit without changes, as disclosure of AI use satisfies the quality assurance requirement.

options.label: D
options.text: Ask the AI to revise the section by providing the correct guarantee structure details, including the specific deal terms, to get a more accurate draft.

question_text: Which of the following inputs is safe to include verbatim in a Copilot prompt without any abstraction or modification?
scenario_text: You are an Analyst preparing a sector overview for a client briefing. You have several documents on your desk: an internal credit risk rating memo for a corporate client, a published annual report from a publicly listed company, a draft strategy document from your team, and a third-party embargoed research report. You need to use Copilot to help synthesise background information.

options.label: A
options.text: The published annual report of the publicly listed company, sourced from its investor relations website.

options.label: B
options.text: The internal credit risk rating memo, because it is already stored in your organisation's secure drive.

options.label: C
options.text: The embargoed third-party research report, because it contains sector-level data rather than client-specific data.

options.label: D
options.text: The draft strategy document, because it has not yet been formally classified as confidential.

question_text: Review the Copilot prompt below. Identify its weaknesses as a strategic prompt, then rewrite it to be significantly more effective for the analyst's stated purpose.
scenario_text:
An Analyst at Northgate Advisory submitted this Copilot prompt to help prepare for a client meeting:

---
"Tell me about the mining sector."
---

The analyst's actual goal was to prepare a five-minute verbal briefing for a relationship manager who is meeting a mid-sized copper mining company to discuss potential export financing. The briefing should cover current commodity price trends, key operational risks, and one or two talking points relevant to export financing conversations.

criteria.name: Weakness diagnosis
criteria.description: Correctly identifies at least two weaknesses in the original prompt: it is too broad/vague, specifies no audience or purpose, defines no output format, and provides no analytical focus or scope.

criteria.name: Role and context added
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt specifies a role for Copilot and provides relevant context (e.g., preparing a verbal briefing for a relationship manager meeting a copper mining company to discuss export financing).

criteria.name: Format and scope defined
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt specifies the output format (e.g., a concise verbal briefing outline or bullet points) and scope (e.g., commodity price trends, operational risks, export financing talking points).

criteria.name: Overall improvement in strategic quality
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt is substantially more likely to produce a useful, targeted output than the original — it is specific, purposeful, and calibrated to the analyst's actual workflow need.

question_text: An Analyst uses Copilot to generate a summary of financial risk indicators for a sector report. Which action best reflects critical evaluation of the AI output before it is used in a client-facing document?
scenario_text: You are an Analyst at Harlow Financial Group. You used Copilot to generate a paragraph summarising key financial risk indicators for the commercial real estate sector. The output reads fluently and cites what appear to be specific statistics (e.g., 'vacancy rates rose to 18.4% in Q2' and 'debt-service coverage ratios fell below 1.2x for 34% of loans'). You are about to paste this paragraph into a sector briefing note that will be shared with clients.

options.label: A
options.text: Verify the specific statistics against the original source documents or authoritative databases before including them, and flag any figures that cannot be confirmed.

options.label: B
options.text: Accept the output as accurate because Copilot is connected to organisational data and would not fabricate statistics.

options.label: C
options.text: Lightly edit the paragraph for tone and include it, since the figures are plausible and consistent with general market knowledge.

options.label: D
options.text: Ask Copilot to regenerate the paragraph twice more and use the version that appears most consistent across the three outputs.

question_text: Review the AI-generated data interpretation below. Identify any analytical errors, unsupported conclusions, or data reasoning problems, and explain what the analyst should do before using this output in a portfolio review.
scenario_text:
An Analyst asked Copilot to analyse five years of EBITDA margin data for 40 industrial manufacturers. Copilot returned the following interpretation:

---
'Analysis of the dataset shows that EBITDA margins across the sector have improved steadily by an average of 2.3 percentage points per year over the five-year period. This confirms that the industrial manufacturing sector is in a strong growth phase and presents low credit risk overall. Three companies — Ferrotek Industries, Caldwell Precision, and Morrow Components — show margins significantly below the sector average and should be immediately flagged as high credit risk and removed from the portfolio. The trend is consistent and unlikely to reverse given current macroeconomic conditions.'
---

Your task: Identify all analytical and reasoning problems in this output, and specify what steps the analyst should take before acting on these findings.

criteria.name: Analytical errors identified
criteria.description: Identifies at least two analytical errors: (1) conflating EBITDA margin improvement with 'low credit risk overall' — margin is one indicator, not a complete credit assessment; (2) the conclusion that below-average margin alone justifies 'high credit risk' and immediate portfolio removal is an unsupported leap; (3) the forward-looking claim about macroeconomic conditions is speculative and unsourced.

criteria.name: Reasoning problems flagged
criteria.description: Flags that Copilot has made a definitive recommendation (remove companies from portfolio) that exceeds its appropriate role — AI should surface patterns for analyst review, not make portfolio decisions — and that the output presents speculation as certainty.

criteria.name: Corrective analyst steps specified
criteria.description: Specifies at least two concrete steps the analyst should take before acting: e.g., verify the 2.3pp average figure against the raw data, conduct a fuller credit assessment of the three flagged companies using multiple indicators, and treat the macroeconomic claim as unverified.

question_text: An Analyst is asked to use AI to help prepare a relationship intelligence briefing ahead of a client meeting. Which approach best demonstrates responsible and effective use of AI for this task?
scenario_text: You are an Analyst at Harlow Financial Group supporting a relationship manager who has a first meeting next week with Solaris Packaging Inc., a mid-sized manufacturer. The relationship manager wants a briefing note covering the company's recent business developments, key decision-makers, and any publicly known strategic priorities. You have access to Copilot and a range of public sources.

options.label: A
options.text: Use Copilot to synthesise publicly available information (press releases, news articles, published financials) into a structured briefing note, then verify key facts and add analyst commentary before sharing with the relationship manager.

options.label: B
options.text: Export the client's CRM interaction history and financial exposure data into Copilot to generate a comprehensive briefing that includes internal relationship notes.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask Copilot to generate a full briefing note from memory without providing any source documents, since it has broad knowledge of business and industry.

options.label: D
options.text: Use Copilot only to format and proofread a briefing note you have already written manually, since AI should not be involved in relationship intelligence tasks.

question_text: An Analyst uses Copilot to draft a client-facing briefing note. Which approach best reflects responsible and effective use of AI for professional communication?
scenario_text: You are an Analyst at Northgate Advisory. Your director has asked you to produce a two-page briefing note for a corporate client summarising recent developments in the global shipping and logistics sector. You use Copilot to generate a first draft based on publicly available sources. The draft is well-structured and reads fluently, but you have not yet reviewed it in detail.

options.label: A
options.text: Review the draft carefully for factual accuracy, tone appropriateness, and any claims that need verification or caveating, then edit and personalise it before sending to the client.

options.label: B
options.text: Send the Copilot draft directly to the client, since it is based on public sources and reads professionally.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask Copilot to review its own draft for errors and send the revised version without further analyst review.

options.label: D
options.text: Discard the Copilot draft and write the briefing note entirely from scratch to ensure full ownership of the content.

question_text: Which of the following inputs is SAFE to paste directly into a non-approved external AI tool when drafting a follow-up email campaign?
scenario_text: You attended the Northgate Exporters Summit on behalf of your organisation and collected a spreadsheet of 200 leads including names, emails, job titles, company names, and conversation notes. You want to use an AI writing tool to help draft a personalised follow-up email series. You also have access to an internal campaign performance report, a publicly available industry outlook on clean energy exports, and your organisation's approved brand messaging guide (marked 'Internal Use Only').

options.label: A
options.text: The publicly available industry outlook on clean energy exports, referenced only for sector context with no lead details included.

options.label: B
options.text: The full lead spreadsheet, because the contacts gave their business cards voluntarily at the event.

options.label: C
options.text: The internal campaign performance report, because it contains no client financial data.

options.label: D
options.text: The brand messaging guide marked 'Internal Use Only', because it will help the AI match your tone.

question_text: Write a prompt you would use in an approved AI tool to draft a follow-up email for trade show leads — without exposing any personally identifiable or non-public information.
scenario_text: You collected 200 leads at the Westport Composites trade show. The spreadsheet includes names, emails, job titles, company names, and brief conversation notes. You want to use your organisation's approved AI writing assistant to draft a follow-up email that highlights export financing support for manufacturers. You must not include any personal details, real company names, or unpublished internal data in your prompt.

criteria.name: PII Exclusion
criteria.description: The prompt contains no real names, email addresses, company names, or other personally identifiable information from the lead list.

criteria.name: Contextual Utility
criteria.description: The prompt provides enough context (audience type, purpose, key message) for the AI to generate a useful and relevant draft email.

criteria.name: Role and Audience Framing
criteria.description: The prompt clearly specifies the intended audience (e.g. manufacturers exploring export financing) and the desired tone or format.

criteria.name: Policy Awareness
criteria.description: The prompt includes or implies a constraint that keeps the output appropriate for external use (e.g. no confidential claims, no specific financial promises, or a note to flag for review).

question_text: Review the AI prompt below and identify all responsible AI problems. Then rewrite the prompt so it is safe to use in a non-approved external AI tool.
scenario_text:
A colleague on your marketing team drafted the following prompt to generate a nurture email:

---
"Here is our lead list from the Harborview Agri-Tech Expo. Key contacts include Sandra Okonkwo (VP Procurement, Greenfield Grains Ltd, sandra.o@greenfield.ca) and Marcus Tieu (Export Manager, Tieu Family Farms, m.tieu@tieufarms.com). Our internal campaign code is AGRI-Q3-2025 and our target conversion rate is 12% (not yet public). Please write a personalised follow-up email for each contact referencing their conversation notes and encouraging them to book a call with our trade advisor."
---

Task: (1) List every responsible AI problem in this prompt. (2) Rewrite the prompt so it is safe to use while still producing a useful email draft.

criteria.name: Problem Identification — PII
criteria.description: Correctly identifies that real names, email addresses, and company names are personally identifiable information that should not be entered into a non-approved external AI tool.

criteria.name: Problem Identification — Non-Public Internal Data
criteria.description: Correctly identifies that the internal campaign code and unpublished conversion rate target are non-public organisational data that must not be shared externally.

criteria.name: Rewrite — PII Removed
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt replaces all real names, emails, and company names with generic descriptors (e.g. 'a VP of Procurement at a mid-sized grain exporter') and removes the internal campaign code and conversion figure.

criteria.name: Rewrite — Utility Preserved
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt still provides sufficient context (audience role, industry, purpose, desired action) for the AI to generate a useful and relevant follow-up email draft.

question_text: Which prompting technique would MOST improve the relevance and quality of AI-generated copy for a niche B2B audience?
scenario_text: You are developing a content series targeting CFOs at mid-sized Canadian agri-food exporters. You want to use an approved AI writing tool to draft LinkedIn posts that speak directly to this audience's pain points around currency risk and export financing. Your first draft prompt produced generic financial content that did not resonate with the agri-food sector.

options.label: A
options.text: Add audience persona details, industry-specific pain points, and a sample tone or example post to the prompt so the AI has richer context to work from.

options.label: B
options.text: Ask the AI to make the post 'more professional and detailed' without changing any other part of the prompt.

options.label: C
options.text: Run the same prompt multiple times and select whichever output sounds best.

options.label: D
options.text: Switch to a different AI tool, since the current one is not capable of producing sector-specific content.

question_text: Write a strategic prompt to generate a LinkedIn post targeting a specific B2B audience segment for a trade finance awareness campaign.
scenario_text: Your organisation is running a campaign to raise awareness of export credit solutions among operations directors at small and medium-sized Canadian tech hardware manufacturers. You want to use an approved AI tool to draft a LinkedIn post (150–200 words) that speaks to their concern about getting paid on time when selling to international buyers. The post should be informative, not salesy, and end with a soft call to action.

criteria.name: Audience Specificity
criteria.description: The prompt clearly defines the target audience including their role, industry, and a relevant pain point or concern (e.g. payment risk on international sales).

criteria.name: Output Constraints
criteria.description: The prompt specifies format requirements such as word count, platform (LinkedIn), tone (informative, not salesy), and the desired call to action.

criteria.name: Strategic Framing
criteria.description: The prompt frames the content goal strategically — e.g. building awareness or trust rather than direct selling — and communicates this intent to the AI.

criteria.name: Prompt Clarity and Structure
criteria.description: The prompt is clearly structured, unambiguous, and provides enough context for the AI to produce a relevant first draft without requiring significant follow-up clarification.

question_text: Analyse the weak prompt below and rewrite it as a high-quality strategic prompt that would produce better marketing copy for the described scenario.
scenario_text:
A marketing coordinator submitted the following prompt to generate an email for a campaign:

---
"Write a marketing email about our services."
---

Context you have available: The email is for a re-engagement campaign targeting lapsed newsletter subscribers who are export managers at Canadian forestry companies. The goal is to remind them of trade risk advisory resources and encourage them to re-subscribe. The tone should be warm and professional, and the email should be under 200 words with a clear CTA button label.

Task: (1) Identify at least three specific weaknesses in the original prompt. (2) Rewrite it as a strategic prompt using the context provided.

criteria.name: Weakness Identification
criteria.description: Identifies at least three specific weaknesses in the original prompt (e.g. no audience defined, no goal stated, no tone specified, no format constraints, no subject matter context).

criteria.name: Audience and Goal in Rewrite
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt explicitly names the target audience (lapsed subscribers, export managers, forestry sector) and the campaign goal (re-engagement, re-subscription).

criteria.name: Tone, Format, and CTA in Rewrite
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt specifies tone (warm, professional), word limit (under 200 words), and requests a clear CTA button label.

criteria.name: Content Direction in Rewrite
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt directs the AI toward the relevant subject matter — trade risk advisory resources — giving the AI enough substance to produce a relevant and useful draft.

question_text: An AI tool has generated a statistic for use in a thought leadership article. What is the MOST appropriate next step before publishing?
scenario_text: You asked an approved AI writing assistant to help draft a thought leadership article on supply chain resilience for Canadian exporters. The AI produced the following sentence: 'According to recent industry research, 67% of Canadian SME exporters experienced at least one critical supply chain disruption in the past 18 months.' You do not recognise this statistic from any source you provided, and the AI did not cite a reference.

options.label: A
options.text: Verify the statistic against a credible, traceable source before including it; if no source can be confirmed, remove or replace it with a verified figure.

options.label: B
options.text: Keep the statistic because it sounds plausible and aligns with the article's argument.

options.label: C
options.text: Add a footnote saying 'Source: AI-generated' so readers know where it came from.

options.label: D
options.text: Ask the AI to provide its source, and publish the article once the AI confirms the figure.

question_text: Write a prompt that instructs an AI tool to help you critically review a draft marketing article for factual accuracy, brand alignment, and potential bias — before it is published.
scenario_text: Your team has drafted a 600-word article on the benefits of export credit insurance for Canadian women-owned businesses entering new markets. Before publishing, you want to use an approved AI tool to help you identify any unsupported claims, language that may unintentionally stereotype or exclude, and messaging that may not align with your organisation's inclusive and balanced brand voice. You will still do a final human review, but want AI to flag issues first.

criteria.name: Factual Accuracy Check
criteria.description: The prompt explicitly asks the AI to flag unsupported claims, unverified statistics, or assertions that would require a cited source.

criteria.name: Bias and Inclusivity Check
criteria.description: The prompt asks the AI to identify language that may stereotype, exclude, or unintentionally marginalise any group, particularly given the article's focus on women-owned businesses.

criteria.name: Brand Voice Alignment
criteria.description: The prompt asks the AI to assess whether the tone and messaging align with a defined brand standard (e.g. inclusive, balanced, professional) rather than just asking for general editing.

criteria.name: Human Review Framing
criteria.description: The prompt frames the AI's role as a first-pass reviewer and either explicitly notes that a human will make final decisions or asks the AI to present findings as suggestions rather than corrections.

question_text: Review the AI-generated marketing copy excerpt below. Identify all critical evaluation concerns and explain what action should be taken for each.
scenario_text:
Your AI writing tool produced the following excerpt for a campaign landing page targeting Canadian cleantech exporters:

---
"Veridia Trade Solutions has helped over 10,000 Canadian exporters unlock $4.2 billion in new international revenue since 2018. Our AI-powered platform is trusted by virtually every major cleantech firm in Canada. Studies show that companies using trade finance tools grow 3x faster than those that don't. Don't get left behind — join the exporters who are already winning."
---

Task: Identify every critical evaluation concern in this excerpt (e.g. unverified claims, vague language, potentially misleading statements, tone issues) and state what action should be taken for each concern.

criteria.name: Unverified Quantitative Claims
criteria.description: Identifies that '10,000 exporters', '$4.2 billion', and '3x faster growth' are specific figures with no cited source, and recommends verifying against traceable data or removing/qualifying them.

criteria.name: Vague or Misleading Language
criteria.description: Identifies 'virtually every major cleantech firm' as an unsubstantiated superlative and 'studies show' as a vague attribution, and recommends replacing with specific, verifiable references or removing the claims.

criteria.name: Tone and Brand Alignment
criteria.description: Flags 'Don't get left behind' and 'already winning' as fear-based or competitive language that may not align with a professional, inclusive brand voice, and recommends revising to a more empowering or informative tone.

question_text: How should a marketing manager BEST use AI to prepare for a stakeholder briefing with a key regional partner, while respecting information boundaries?
scenario_text: You are preparing for a quarterly briefing with Meridian Trade Alliance, a regional industry association that co-promotes your organisation's export programs to its 500+ member companies. You want to use AI to help you prepare talking points, anticipate their questions, and identify opportunities to deepen the partnership. You have access to publicly available information about Meridian, your organisation's internal partnership notes (marked confidential), and past co-branded campaign results.

options.label: A
options.text: Use AI to synthesise publicly available information about Meridian and draft talking points and anticipated questions, keeping internal confidential notes out of any non-approved AI tool.

options.label: B
options.text: Paste the full internal partnership notes into the AI tool so it can generate the most personalised and accurate briefing preparation possible.

options.label: C
options.text: Skip AI preparation entirely for stakeholder briefings, as relationship intelligence is too sensitive for AI involvement.

options.label: D
options.text: Use AI to draft a script for the entire meeting and read from it verbatim to ensure consistency.

question_text: Write a prompt to help you use AI to prepare personalised outreach messaging for a key industry partner, based only on publicly available information.
scenario_text: You are preparing outreach to Cascadia Exporters Network, a regional trade association whose members are primarily small and medium-sized manufacturers in the Pacific region. You want to invite them to co-host a webinar on accessing international markets. You have reviewed their public website, recent press releases, and their published annual priorities. You want AI to help you draft a personalised outreach email that references their known priorities and frames the webinar as mutually beneficial — without using any internal CRM notes or confidential relationship history.

criteria.name: Public Information Grounding
criteria.description: The prompt explicitly states that the AI should base its output only on publicly available information provided in the prompt (e.g. website priorities, press releases) and does not reference or request use of internal CRM or confidential data.

criteria.name: Partner Personalisation
criteria.description: The prompt includes specific details about the partner's known public priorities or audience so the AI can tailor the outreach meaningfully rather than producing a generic invitation.

criteria.name: Mutual Benefit Framing
criteria.description: The prompt instructs the AI to frame the webinar invitation in terms of value for both parties, not just as a promotional ask.

criteria.name: Tone and Format Guidance
criteria.description: The prompt specifies the desired tone (e.g. collegial, professional) and format (e.g. email, approximate length, key sections) to guide the AI toward a usable output.

question_text: Review the AI-assisted partner briefing note below. Identify any relationship intelligence concerns and suggest specific improvements.
scenario_text:
A colleague used an AI tool to draft the following briefing note ahead of a meeting with Pinnacle Agri-Export Council, a key industry association partner:

---
**Partner Briefing: Pinnacle Agri-Export Council**
Pinnacle represents approximately 300 agri-food exporters. They are probably interested in trade finance because most small exporters struggle with cash flow. Their leadership likely wants more visibility for their association. We should offer them a co-branding deal and mention that our last partner, Harborview Growers Alliance, was very happy with the arrangement. Use this to pressure them into agreeing quickly.
---

Task: Identify all relationship intelligence concerns in this briefing note (e.g. assumptions presented as facts, inappropriate references, problematic tactics) and recommend specific corrections for each.

criteria.name: Assumption vs. Evidence
criteria.description: Identifies that 'probably interested' and 'likely wants' are unverified assumptions presented as intelligence, and recommends grounding claims in confirmed public information or flagging them as hypotheses to be validated.

criteria.name: Inappropriate Partner Reference
criteria.description: Identifies that referencing Harborview Growers Alliance's satisfaction without their consent may breach confidentiality or relationship trust, and recommends removing or obtaining permission before referencing other partners.

criteria.name: Problematic Negotiation Tactic
criteria.description: Identifies 'pressure them into agreeing quickly' as an inappropriate and potentially relationship-damaging tactic, and recommends replacing it with a collaborative, value-based engagement approach.

criteria.name: Overall Briefing Quality
criteria.description: Recommends that the briefing note be revised to reflect verified public information, a respectful partnership framing, and a clear mutual-value proposition before the meeting.

question_text: A marketing manager wants to use AI to analyse campaign performance data and recommend budget reallocation. Which approach BEST reflects sound data-informed decision-making?
scenario_text: Your team ran a multi-channel awareness campaign last quarter across email, LinkedIn, and webinars. You have a dashboard showing open rates, click-through rates, registration numbers, and cost-per-lead for each channel. You want to use an approved AI tool to help interpret the data and recommend where to shift budget for the next quarter. The AI produces a recommendation to cut the webinar budget by 40% and double LinkedIn spend.

options.label: A
options.text: Use the AI recommendation as a starting point, but cross-check it against your strategic priorities, audience quality data, and any contextual factors the AI may not have had access to before making a final decision.

options.label: B
options.text: Implement the AI recommendation immediately, since it is based on the full dataset and is therefore more objective than human judgement.

options.label: C
options.text: Reject the AI recommendation entirely, because budget decisions should never involve AI analysis.

options.label: D
options.text: Ask the AI to run the analysis again with a different prompt until it recommends keeping the current budget allocation.

question_text: Write a prompt to help you use AI to interpret campaign performance data and surface insights to inform a budget recommendation — without uploading raw data files.
scenario_text: You have just completed a quarter-long lead generation campaign targeting Canadian agri-food exporters across three channels: email newsletter (2,400 sends, 18% open rate, 3.2% CTR, 42 leads, $28 cost-per-lead), LinkedIn sponsored posts (budget $4,000, 310 clicks, 18 leads, $222 cost-per-lead), and a virtual roundtable event (80 registrants, 54 attendees, 12 qualified leads, $167 cost-per-lead). You want to use an approved AI tool to help you interpret these results and draft a data-informed recommendation for next quarter's budget split. You will type the data directly into the prompt rather than uploading any files.

criteria.name: Data Inclusion in Prompt
criteria.description: The prompt includes the key performance figures typed directly (not as a file upload), giving the AI sufficient data to perform a meaningful comparison across channels.

criteria.name: Analytical Task Clarity
criteria.description: The prompt clearly asks the AI to compare channel efficiency (e.g. cost-per-lead, lead quality indicators) and identify which channels performed best relative to the campaign goal.

criteria.name: Decision Support Framing
criteria.description: The prompt asks the AI to produce a recommendation or options for budget reallocation, framed as input for human decision-making rather than a final directive.

criteria.name: Contextual Constraints
criteria.description: The prompt includes at least one contextual constraint or consideration for the AI to factor in (e.g. audience quality, strategic priorities, channel fit for the target segment).

question_text: Review the AI-generated campaign insight summary below. Identify any data interpretation problems and explain what a more rigorous analysis would consider.
scenario_text:
A marketing analyst used an AI tool to summarise campaign results and produced the following insight note:

---
**Q2 Campaign Insight Summary**
The email channel was the clear winner this quarter with the highest number of leads (42). LinkedIn underperformed with only 18 leads and should be cut from next quarter's plan. The virtual roundtable was average. Overall, the campaign was a success because we exceeded our lead volume target of 60 leads (actual: 72 leads total).
---

Task: Identify all data interpretation problems in this summary and explain what a more rigorous, data-informed analysis would need to consider.

criteria.name: Cost Efficiency Omission
criteria.description: Identifies that the summary judges channel performance by lead volume alone without considering cost-per-lead (email: $28, LinkedIn: $222, roundtable: $167), which significantly changes the relative performance picture.

criteria.name: Lead Quality Not Considered
criteria.description: Identifies that raw lead counts do not reflect lead quality or conversion potential, and that the roundtable's 12 'qualified leads' may represent higher value than the email channel's 42 unqualified leads.

criteria.name: Premature Channel Elimination
criteria.description: Identifies that recommending LinkedIn be cut based on one quarter of volume data is premature without considering audience reach, brand awareness value, or longer-term pipeline contribution.

criteria.name: Success Metric Limitation
criteria.description: Identifies that declaring the campaign 'a success' solely because total lead volume exceeded target ignores other dimensions such as cost efficiency, lead quality, and channel mix effectiveness.

question_text: Which approach BEST describes how AI should be used to enhance — rather than replace — a marketing manager's communication of a complex policy message to an external audience?
scenario_text: Your organisation is launching a new export guarantee program with several eligibility conditions and application steps. You need to communicate this to a broad audience of Canadian SME exporters through a blog post, a social media series, and an FAQ document. You have a detailed internal policy brief that explains the program accurately but is written in technical language. You want to use AI to help produce the external-facing communications.

options.label: A
options.text: Use AI to translate the technical policy brief into plain-language drafts for each format, then review and edit each output to ensure accuracy, appropriate tone, and alignment with approved messaging before publishing.

options.label: B
options.text: Publish the AI-generated drafts directly without review, since the AI was given the accurate source document.

options.label: C
options.text: Use AI only to check spelling and grammar, and write all substantive content manually to avoid any risk of inaccuracy.

options.label: D
options.text: Ask the AI to simplify the policy brief into one universal message and use that single message across all three formats without adaptation.

question_text: Write a prompt to use AI to adapt a technical program description into an engaging, plain-language social media post for a specific audience.
scenario_text: Your organisation has just launched the Accelerate Export Guarantee Program, which provides up to $2M in credit guarantees for eligible Canadian SMEs exporting to emerging markets. The internal program description is written in policy language and includes terms like 'obligor risk threshold', 'indemnification ceiling', and 'drawdown conditions'. You want to use an approved AI tool to adapt this into a LinkedIn post (under 150 words) for an audience of first-time exporters who are unfamiliar with trade finance terminology. The post should be encouraging, jargon-free, and end with a clear call to action to learn more.

criteria.name: Plain Language Instruction
criteria.description: The prompt explicitly instructs the AI to avoid jargon or technical trade finance terms and to use plain, accessible language appropriate for first-time exporters.

criteria.name: Audience and Platform Fit
criteria.description: The prompt specifies the target audience (first-time exporters, unfamiliar with trade finance) and the platform (LinkedIn), enabling the AI to calibrate tone and format appropriately.

criteria.name: Key Message Preservation
criteria.description: The prompt includes the core program details (credit guarantee, up to $2M, Canadian SMEs, emerging markets) so the AI can produce an accurate and informative post rather than a vague one.

criteria.name: Format and CTA Requirements
criteria.description: The prompt specifies the word limit (under 150 words), desired tone (encouraging), and the requirement for a clear call to action at the end.

question_text: Review the AI-generated communications excerpt below. Identify all augmented communication problems and rewrite the excerpt to address them.
scenario_text:
A marketing coordinator used an AI tool to draft the following LinkedIn post to announce a new export advisory service:

---
"Attention exporters. Our new service will solve all your international trade problems. Whether you're dealing with currency issues, buyer defaults, or regulatory nightmares, we have the answer. Every exporter who has used our advisory services has seen significant improvements. Book a call today and transform your export business forever."
---

Task: (1) Identify all augmented communication problems in this post (e.g. overclaiming, vague language, tone issues, unverifiable assertions). (2) Rewrite the post as a concise, credible, and audience-appropriate LinkedIn announcement of approximately 80–100 words.

criteria.name: Problem Identification
criteria.description: Identifies at least three specific problems: overclaiming ('solve all your problems', 'transform your export business forever'), unverifiable universal assertion ('every exporter has seen significant improvements'), vague benefit language, and/or an alarmist tone ('regulatory nightmares') inconsistent with a professional brand voice.

criteria.name: Rewrite — Credibility and Accuracy
criteria.description: The rewritten post removes overclaims and unverifiable assertions, replacing them with specific, honest, and credible language about what the advisory service offers.

criteria.name: Rewrite — Tone, Format, and CTA
criteria.description: The rewritten post uses a professional and encouraging tone appropriate for LinkedIn, stays within approximately 80–100 words, and includes a clear and proportionate call to action.
